title: Measuring forecast error: MAE, RMSE and MAPE

videos.script: Two forecasts of the same weeks. Which one is better? {{two}} The question sounds simple and it hides a choice. Better on average? Better on the worst week? Better in orders, or in per cent? {{choice}} Each of those is a different number, and they can disagree. In this lesson they do. {{disagree}} MAE is the average miss, in orders. RMSE squares the misses first, so one big miss counts for a lot. MAPE turns each miss into a percentage of what happened, so a series of thousands and a series of tens can be compared. {{three}} Each one is right for some decision and misleading for another. {{decision}} And each one, measured on one stretch of weeks, is one draw. Measure again from another starting week and the winner can change. {{draw}} By the end you will have measured every forecast of lesson 3 against the same six months, and you will know which number to quote, and when not to trust it. {{end}}
